title: Prove the (2,0,1,1) three-frame profile admits no seven-call word.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped character proof. No new κ and no word.

In the PR2085/2112 formal register model, the seven-call profile `(a,b,p,q,r,s,t) = (2,0,1,1,1,1,1)` admits no word. The determinant equation is `R+S+T = A+3B = diag(1,3)`. Every decomposition into three nonzero symmetric rational rank-one matrices admits an AB or PQ character that detects two calls and four targets. The selected record stays κ = `781451/250000000`.

This is a proof for this one named census profile. It is not a multiplication theorem, not an exhaustive census of the other profiles, and not a heuristic search. Rational solutions of the matrix equation exist; `2B+P+Q` is one, and the same character excludes it. The other eighteen three-frame census profiles, and every decomposition with four or more added frames, remain open. The settled profiles `(1,1,1,1)/(1,1,1)` and `(0,2,1,1)/(1,1,1)` are not redone.

The bilinear form is `3 x1 y1 + x2 y2`. The constants 3, 6, and 12 used for `3A+B` in the `(0,2,1,1)` argument do not transfer unchanged. The axis equation here is `(α-2l) v1^2 (αβ-γ^2 - 6α k) = 2 α^2 k v2^2`.

## Task and overlap

Session r165. The assigned question is the named sibling three-frame profile `(2,0,1,1)/(1,1,1)` from the open next question of PR #7013. The residual is `diag(1,3)`.

Base commit: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (upstream CrocSwap main, re-fetched 2026-11-10 and unchanged). The fork PR base is `cursor/upstream-17469fff-pin-e6bb`, which points at that commit. Priority revision 8. The priority file still quotes an older selected decimal; the frontier value used here is the selected record.

Task card: `bit-new-register-model`, `scope_status: changed`. The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers one profile left open by the `(0,2,1,1)` exclusion.

Overlap recheck on 2026-11-10, with `scripts/find_overlap.py --refresh` against open upstream PRs and discussion #1166 (6971 comment/reply records, complete pagination): the string `(2,0,1,1)` occurs in the census comment 19377345, in the #7013 finding comment 19507678, and in the #7013 PR body. All three name the profile as open. No open PR settles it. A separate `diag(1,3)` hit in `research/tensor-helper-capacity` is an unrelated tensor-capacity statement. No fork branch was already named for this profile.

## Validation

Python 3.12. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/three-signed-a-twice --check-only
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/three-signed-a-twice
python3 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/three-signed-a-twice --ref HEAD --check-modes --check-source-history
```

Observed: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with `outcome=completed`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` at `e0026d8fd0d8c3eef46391e3e3e540c15279eec5`, including source-history pin `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. The direct check is `python3 -I -W error -B research/three-signed-a-twice/verify.py`, also run with `-O`. Both printed `PASS three-signed-a-twice character checks`.

`verify.py` expands the scale-bracket, Cramer-determinant, and axis-rearrangement polynomials and checks that each identity is exact. It exhausts the 32 odd residue classes of the mod-8 discriminant lemma, checks the new axis residues for `6αk` and for `2 α^2 k v2^2`, checks the diagonal and axial quadratic valuations of `3 x1^2 + x2^2`, and checks the strict valuation gaps in both mixed orientations. It then checks explicit characters on five declared frames: the rational solution `2B+P+Q`, a negative frame with scales `(7, 6, -3)`, a fractional frame, a parallel opposite-scale pair, and a frame equal to the old matrix `A`. Each witness detects two calls and four targets. Failure controls reject a tampered sum, reject `I` as a rank-one summand, reject an even-even-even form, and reject the `diag(3,1)` bilinear form as a solution of this residual. The single-line box and the axis-reduction box are finite corroborations. They are not the proof; Sections 4 through 6 of `PROOF.md` are.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the selected-result cold replay, and `scripts/research_selected_baseline.py`.

## Credit

The register model is Cinna Davis's PR2085/2112 formal model. The determinant and first-order inequality are the PR2910 package as recorded in apoursh's two-signed-frame floor, PR #6190. The census is discussion comment 19377345. The released all-old-once handoff is comment 19377832. The `(0,2,1,1)` exclusion and the question answered here are unpaidmoon PR #7013. The all-old-once profile was character-excluded separately and is not redone here.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. No independent human or formal-kernel review. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Which of the other eighteen three-frame count profiles survive the same test? A useful first step is to read one tuple that discussion comment 19377345 already prints, other than `(1,1,1,1)`, `(0,2,1,1)`, and `(2,0,1,1)`, write that tuple's own determinant residual, and test one rational rank-one solution with the bilinear form of that residual. This package does not name another tuple. The forms `3 x1 y1 + x2 y2` and `x1 y1 + 3 x2 y2` are special to `diag(1,3)` and `diag(3,1)`.

Four or more added signed rank-one frames are outside this three-summand character and are not a next question of this package.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The predecessor states the sibling residual and warns that the constants do not transfer. Recomputing the bracket, the axis equation, and the Cramer matrix from `diag(1,3)`, and checking those polynomials in the verifier, is enough to keep the two profiles apart. Linking this once in discussion #1200 is enough.
